answers.explanation: The signal runs on the inner conductor, the insulator keeps it apart from the shield, the shield blocks noise, and the jacket protects it all.
Polyethylene: low signal loss, water-resistant, sturdy, and cheap.
The shield is why coax resists interference better than plain wire.
Along with protecting the cable from damage, moisture, dust, chemicals, heat, and short circuits.
Baseband puts one signal directly onto the wire. It's simple, and used inside a building's LAN.
Broadband coax divides the cable's frequencies into many channels, so TV and Internet travel at once.
Frequency-division multiplexing: like radio stations sharing the air on different frequencies.
Time-division multiplexing: each device gets its own slice of time on the single channel.
Broadband relies on modulation. Baseband uses none.
Baseband has limited bandwidth: one channel, no frequency multiplexing, no modulation.
